# OMIX Journal — Publication and Article Index

The OMIX Journal is published by OMIX Digital Solutions. It is a company-owned technical publication, not an independent news outlet. Product and company relationships are disclosed in relevant articles.

## Editorial standards
The publication aims to explain a specific reader problem, state assumptions and limitations, use primary references, verify technical examples where feasible, correct material errors, and avoid fabricated benchmarks or credentials. AI-assisted tools may support research or editing, but a human editor is responsible for factual and technical review.

Read the [Editorial Policy](https://blog.omixsystems.store/editorial-policy), [About page](https://blog.omixsystems.store/about), [Privacy Policy](https://blog.omixsystems.store/privacy), and [Terms of Use](https://blog.omixsystems.store/terms).

## Articles

### Designing Modular Software Systems: Boundaries, Contracts, and Change
https://blog.omixsystems.store/wiki/modular-software-systems

Explains how to define module responsibilities, choose boundaries around change, make interfaces explicit, establish data ownership, handle failures, and test contracts. It distinguishes modular monoliths from service decomposition and emphasizes proportionate architecture.

### AI Model Routing: Designing a Gateway Between Applications and Providers
https://blog.omixsystems.store/wiki/introducing-bifrost

Explains the model-gateway pattern, provider adapters, routing policies, timeouts, bounded retries, fallback compatibility, credential protection, usage measurement and staged implementation. It does not claim that every described capability is currently deployed in Bifrost.

### Designing Reliable Webhook Consumers: Idempotency, Retries, and Reconciliation
https://blog.omixsystems.store/wiki/reliable-webhook-consumers

Covers at-least-once delivery, sender verification, durable event records, transactional processing, retry classification, event ordering, dead-letter handling and reconciliation.

### M-PESA STK Push: Designing the Payment Lifecycle Around Asynchronous Callbacks
https://blog.omixsystems.store/wiki/mpesa-stk-push-payment-lifecycle

Explains why payment initiation is not proof of settlement, how to separate orders, attempts and ledger entries, model asynchronous states, deduplicate callbacks, handle late success and reconcile with provider records. Readers should verify exact request fields and callback schemas against current Safaricom Daraja documentation.

### Offline-First Business Software: Local Writes, Sync Queues, and Conflict Resolution
https://blog.omixsystems.store/wiki/offline-first-business-software

Covers workflow selection, durable local persistence, outbox synchronization, idempotent server operations, conflict resolution, server-side authorization, unreliable network behavior and rollout testing.

### Designing SMS Commerce for Feature Phones: Sessions, State Machines, and Payment Events
https://blog.omixsystems.store/wiki/sms-commerce-feature-phone-architecture

A first-party architecture proposal for feature-phone shopping over SMS. It covers session state machines, command parsing, concise product search, separate order and payment records, idempotent callbacks, delivery notifications, opt-out handling, rate limits and pilot testing. It is explicitly labelled as a proposal, not a claim that an SMS commerce channel is currently live.
